author: @luigifranceschi2350
text:
I’m the fleet manager for our company group. We have 50 vehicles. We are located in the alps and we need vehicles that perform well in steep and winding roads. We have decided to slowly pass to electric due to low maintenance, low fuel cost, and also because in the mountain roads the electric cars usually perform really well. They have a nice kick, that is useful to pass slow vehicles, and thanks to regen downhill the advantage on fuel costs becomes even greater than on the flat  compared to ICE, because all the potential energy of an ICE vehicle downhill gets dissipated in heat at the breaks or using the low gears to slow down. while in an EV is put back in the battery.
Or at least this is what Teslas do. We already have one in the fleet. So that is a fact for me.
Due to image issues I wasn’t planning to buy more teslas, and pass to BYD. So I tested 2 of them. Unfortunately the regen is too weak even at the strongest level. I was forced to use the breaks all the way down. And that is bad. Not only because I’m not recovering all the potential energy, but mostly because I risk of overheating the breaks. And that is really bad. So until they don’t come with a more powerful regen setup BYD is a no for us. I really don’t get why BYD doesn’t improve on that part. For the rest are beautiful cars. The interior are far better than teslas and and the cars seems overall more solid and there is a wider choice, so I could have accommodated all the different needs with just one brand, that means just one shop for the maintenance.

author: @TM3PnrbringRecord
text:
I've tested both these cars and I've got to say that many things were wrong in this video. First thing is that the BYD Sealion or any BYD, has no Youtube, Netflix or anything similar integrated into the infotainment system, especially when the screen looks so bad (on all models). You can however use Apple Carplay or Android Auto to mirror it, but the quality is just bad and it will be using your phone's data unlike the Teslas having their own data. On the Tesla, many people still use Netflix, Youtube and the rest while charging, it's not really a gimmick but a comfort. These cars having 14 speakers makes you enjoy films like you're in a cinema, especially late at night when it's darker.

The doors on the Tesla are quite straightforward and I would even say very nice to use. They blend in well with the car's shape and the interior door button is very satisfying to use, seems luxurious but, many new passengers still try to pull on the emergency lever thinking it's the main door lever.
The autonomy, speed, interior space, infotainment, charging prices, aftersales support, quality and how easy it is to drive, all goes to Tesla without a doubt. The things that they messed up like the stalks and the lack of buttons can be fixed with simple aftermarket mods that actually work amazingly well and are very responsive.
Also, driving the Sealion is horrible. It wobbles horribly on corners and it even bounces sometimes when accelerating from 0mph and is unstable. Reminds me much of the Mustang GT Performance, which I also disliked a lot, especially when I actually love Fords.

This video feels very biased against Tesla and could either be a silent sponsorship or politics.

My verdict as an actual car tester: Teslas are great cars, if not, the best on the current market.

author: @MeanMachine1992
text: As an electrical engineer, I laugh every time I hear someone claim a Chinese product is equal to or better than a something made in the US or Germany or France or Japan. If you go through the brands that are used far and wide across industries for simple electrical and electronic needs, you come up with names like Omron, Telemecanique, Siemens, Schneider, GE, Honeywell and so on. A step down would be Hyundai, LS and Delta. If you've ever worked with electrical equipment, servo/step motors or even simple traditional squirrel-cage motors, you'd know the difference between a pure Chinese product and one that comes from a reputable company, even one that has its production line in China. Everything from the ball bearings to the dimensions of the copper wire and in most cases even the copper in the wire itself vastly differ in quality. The end result is that when the damn thing is new, you can see a small difference between the two that can't justifying paying so much more for a reputable brand. But once a year or two passes, you start noticing just how subpar Chinese products really are.

author: @TheEletricboy
text:
Some useful tesla-related advice and recommendations from experience:

1. Mirrors - you can click the steering wheel roller to toggle between left/right mirror.
2. You can add a few quick selection buttons at the bottom of the screen (I like having the seats, steering wheel heating, windshield defog).
3. You can quickly change AC temperature by just swiping left/right with your finger and it you dont have to take your eyes off the road (I even put a "macro" on the left steering wheel scroller which when held for 1s let's me adjust temp by scrolling without taking my hands off the wheel).
4. Android Auto/apple car play - the tesla maps are just the google api so it's exactly the same, plus if you like searching for a favourite saved place on your maps app through your phone you can just click "share" on google maps and select the tesla app, it will send it to your car's screen.
5. Spotify and youtube music come as part of the tesla OS, I don't have the premium versions so I just used a cracked youtube music on my phone and play it through bluetooth, it starts playing as soon as I enter the car so it there's no let-downs from my use case.
6. Suspension - it's one of the most comfortable suspensions I've ever felt (I've only ever had renaults, VWs, older BMWs so it's as close to luxury as my poor ass has ever been).

This is not a hard concept, get it together please. ⁠​⁠​⁠​⁠​⁠​⁠​⁠​⁠@jacksmith-mu3ee 1) The fact that Tesla uses BYD batteries doesn’t mean anything. It doesn’t make the BYD better, and the Tesla is still faster and better to drive despite using BYD batteries.

author: @brighamjb
text:
Ummm, Matt. I normally can really trust your journalism, but I am truly disappointed by the blatant bias in this comparison.

-The interface in the tesla is very intuitive and well optimized. For years it has been vastly superior to any other manufacturer, including your own reviews. Running all of your fingers over the screen to try to imply that is is laggy or unpredictable is very obviously not genuinely trying to use it as intended.
-The lack of Carplay/Android Auto is clearly because the car needs to use it's own nav to to charging planning, so the Tesla approach is comprehensive, whereas the BYD would require jumping back and forth, and most of the time driving longer distances, you would not even be able to use the smartphone connection.
-No mention of the mirrors that dynamically will adjust themselves if you are backing up to show the curb is not even mentioned. Adjusting mirrors should not be done while driving.
-The BYD having a manually adjustable steering column is widely considered to be an economy feature, not a luxurious or positive feature. Almost like if you had handcrank windows, you would not be listing that as a relief like the steering column is implied in this video...

The list goes on of examples in this video. The tesla is faster, brakes better, is better handling and more efficient, the design and interface is of course subjective, but comparing to other vehicles in the industry, the more automated and simplified design is more luxurious than a cluttered and busy design.

Only considering objective details, and then adding the fact it is cheaper and will certainly have better charging and maintenance accessibility, the Model Y objectively wins. Sheep follow despite their better judgement, and the conclusion of this review looks to be sheep-like. This is a disappointment and makes me concerned about your future reviews having political or financial bias rather than objective journalism.

text:
@YokoshimaHake it’s always interesting to see EV guy only consider car ownership as only upfront cost rather than the whole process. Tesla is indeed cheap to maintain in 10 years but Buick, Lincoln, Toyota and other few are only different by less than $500, in 10 years time spawn, (study done by Consumer Report) it’s virtually the same. author: @jeketo
text:
People need to understand that Mat Watson is nowadays an entertainer and not a professional car journalist. I would review this review 2/5.

Winners (picked from video and added some realism):
Boot space+frunk: Tesla
Driving/Handling/Suspension : Tesla
Speed/Acceleration: Tesla
Noise level: Tesla
Infotainment: Tie: Tesla has way better infotainment, but since some people for some reason love CarPlay/Android Auto it should be a tie. Even though you can't use CarPlay/AA for navigation in many cases since it doesnt tell you when to charge. 
Interior: Tie: Tesla has more foot space in the back, a screen in the back and through loading. BYD has more shoulder room with 3 people in the back. BYD has slightly better seats for Mat's preference, but didnt really compain about Tesla seats either. Tesla also has more space for stuff in the front and door pockets are soften.
Charging: Tie, but does BYD even have a possibility to pre-heat the battery for fast charging? Couldnt find answer from the internet, but if not then its a win for Tesla
Buttons: BYD
Range: Tie: I give it a tie just to make people happy. In real world Tesla is a winner here with much better consumpion and real world range, but we go with tie. Moving goal posts to make BYD look better is very unprofessional.

So 4 wins for Tesla and 1 win for BYD. 4 ties. Yet still in the end the car that drives worse, is noisier, has less room, is slower and has worse features for everyday life (driver profiles and manual steering wheel adjustment for example) somehow wins.

And in the end: what a joke with those door handles. Mat suddenly forgot how to use those after first teaching his mother how to use them?

Entertainers logic, not the logic of a professional car journalist. Sadly.

author: @lieutenantjodi
text:
04:21 Let’s talk about car doors.
Specifically, door handles, and how car manufacturers keep fixing problems that never existed. Flush handles? They look cool, sure, but what exactly were they solving? A pull-type handle works perfectly fine. It’s there, it’s simple, and it does the job without needing a sensor, motor, or awkward push-to-pop motion.

Flush handles add steps where there shouldn’t be any. They delay access, fail when the electronics glitch, and make something as basic as opening a door feel like a software update. 

Pull-type handles? Always visible, always ready, always reliable.

In terms of function, speed, and common sense — the pull-type grab handle is still the best and most efficient design.

author: @WEZ4136
text:
@ as we all understand, drivers are different, they have their own individual quirks they do while driving, so for me I vape, so my windows go up and down when I vape, I use my rear wiper, front wiper, indicators, headlights, fogs etc. 
I have spinal damage from an accident while serving in the RAF which means I use the heated seats and adjustable lumbar support, those settings change depending on pain levels, even to moving the seat to find a less painful position. As I use the heated seat a lot I also use the A/C to cool down, even in winter, sometimes I like the air flowing towards my hands, other times towards my face and at times not towards me at all, instead just directed into the car to cool the ambient temperature. 
I’ve been driving through some terrible conditions that have seen the windscreen freezing even long after the car has warmed up and I’m on the move, other times I’ve gone through rain so heavy it’s caused the windscreen to fog up. 
I don’t use cruise control or lane assist, but I do use the physical buttons on the steering wheel to make calls through the voice control which Siri is far superior to the system in cars, as it rarely calls the wrong person whereas the cars voice control system does it too much. 
The only other buttons I use are the sunroof ones and the drive mode one which are easily accessible on the roof and central console respectively, drive mode is used when I come across one of Britains hidden gems of a beautiful winding B road. 
My late grandmother, who taught me to drive (x rally driver) never used anything other than the lights, indicators, heater controls, radio and window winders when she drove. 
This is why every car should have the ability to work for the individual driver, it can’t when they decide that every driver has to do things the same way, especially when it’s a way they have never used, or in my case, I think putting everything into a screen is dangerous especially when using your phone is illegal for the exact same reason.
